questions.stem: Pointing to a man in a photograph, a woman said, 'He is the father of my only son's wife's mother.' How is the man related to the woman?

options.option_text: Father of the woman's son-in-law's mother (son's wife's maternal grandfather indirectly)
Father of the woman's daughter-in-law's mother

questions.explanation: My only son's wife = daughter-in-law. Her mother = daughter-in-law's mother. The father of that mother is the woman's 'daughter-in-law's maternal grandfather' (with respect to the woman, the man is her son's wife's mother's father — equivalent phrasing: father of the woman's daughter-in-law's mother).
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A + B means A is the FATHER of B. A − B means A is the MOTHER of B. A × B means A is the BROTHER of B. Then what does 'P + Q × R − S' mean?

options.option_text: P is the grandfather of S
P is the uncle of S
P is the grandmother of S
P is the father of S

questions.explanation: P + Q ⇒ P is father of Q. Q × R ⇒ Q is brother of R. R − S ⇒ R is mother of S. So R is S's mother; Q is R's brother (S's maternal uncle); P is Q's father — so P is S's maternal GRANDFATHER.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Introducing a girl, Vikas said, 'Her mother is the only daughter of my father-in-law.' How is the girl related to Vikas?
questions.explanation: 'Only daughter of my father-in-law' = Vikas's wife. The girl's mother is Vikas's wife → the girl is Vikas's daughter.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: If M is brother of N, N is sister of O, O is father of P, and P is daughter of Q (female), then how is Q related to M?
questions.explanation: M, N, O are siblings. P is the daughter of O and Q. So Q is O's wife. M is Q's brother-in-law's sibling's wife → Q is M's sister-in-law (brother's wife = bhabhi).
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A is the son of B's father's sister. C is the daughter of B's mother's sister. How is A related to C?
questions.explanation: A is son of B's paternal aunt → A is B's PATERNAL COUSIN. C is daughter of B's maternal aunt → C is B's MATERNAL COUSIN. A and C are cousins to B but NOT to each other (different grandparents). However, in casual / lay usage, A and C are often called 'cousins' through B — so the commonly expected answer is 'cousin'. Strictly, they are unrelated blood-wise. both are B's cousins on opposite sides.
questions.subject: Reasoning

_fixes.was: Cousin (both are B's cousins on opposite sides)
_fixes.moved_to_explanation: both are B's cousins on opposite sides

questions.stem: X is Y's daughter. Z is Y's mother. W is Y's brother's son. How is W related to X?
questions.explanation: Y is X's parent. Y's brother is X's uncle. Y's brother's son (i.e., W) is X's COUSIN. (More precisely, if Y is female, W is X's maternal cousin; if Y is male, W is X's paternal cousin.). specifically, paternal cousin.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A man said, 'That lady is the wife of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the lady related to him?
questions.explanation: 'Only son of my grandfather' = my father. Wife of my father = my mother.
questions.subject: Reasoning
